methodology: Each answer is compared only with an explicit position in the linked party material. Missing or ambiguous positions remain unknown. Parties appear alphabetically, without a score or ranking. These are selected policy questions, not a complete measure of political alignment.

questions.prompt: Should BC expand liquefied natural gas (LNG) development?
questions.yes: Allow new LNG projects and increase production.
questions.note: LNG is natural gas cooled for shipping. Consider export revenue, emissions and electricity demand.

stances.summary: Proposes higher natural gas and LNG production.
Supports new LNG projects and related infrastructure.
Would stop new fossil fuel development.
Would cancel Ksi Lisims LNG and end LNG subsidies.

questions.prompt: Should BC keep restrictions that reserve short-term rentals for a host’s main home?
questions.yes: Keep the main-home rule in communities where it applies.
questions.note: This concerns homes offered for short stays. It does not ban every short-term rental.

stances.summary: Defends provincial short-term rental restrictions.

questions.prompt: Should rent increases be limited when a new tenant moves in?
questions.yes: Tie rent limits to the home, including between tenancies.
questions.no: Let landlords reset rent between tenancies.
questions.note: This is different from the existing annual limit for a tenant who stays in the same home.

stances.summary: Would cap rent increases between tenancies.
Would attach rent controls to the unit.

questions.prompt: Should public transit be free to ride?
questions.no: Keep charging fares to help fund transit.
questions.note: Removing fares needs replacement funding. Service frequency and coverage are separate choices.

stances.summary: Promises fare-free transit.
Proposes free transit and a provincial bus network.

questions.prompt: Should BC allow a separate private-pay health-care option alongside public care?
questions.yes: Allow patients to pay for a separate private care option.
questions.no: Keep access to publicly insured care within the public system.
questions.note: This asks about paying for care covered by the public system, rather than services like cosmetic surgery. Public contracts with private providers are a separate question.

stances.summary: Supports access to private surgery options.
Proposes private care alongside public care.
Rejects privatization and advocates public provision.

questions.prompt: Should BC repeal its Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA)?
questions.note: DRIPA sets a framework for implementing the UN declaration. Repealing it would not remove constitutional or treaty rights.

stances.summary: Would repeal DRIPA.
Would replace DRIPA with another reconciliation framework.
Would repeal DRIPA.
Opposes attacks on the Declaration Act.

questions.prompt: Should schools stop using the SOGI 123 resource package?
questions.note: SOGI means sexual orientation and gender identity. The package provides resources for inclusion and preventing bullying.

stances.summary: Would remove SOGI resources.
Would stop using SOGI 123.
Would remove SOGI 123.
Would implement SOGI 123 across school districts.

questions.prompt: Should drivers be able to choose a private insurer for basic auto coverage?
questions.yes: Open basic insurance to competing providers.
questions.no: Keep ICBC as the sole basic insurance provider.
questions.note: Basic insurance is mandatory coverage. Optional insurance already has competing providers.

stances.summary: Would end ICBC’s monopoly on basic coverage.
Would phase out ICBC’s insurance monopoly.

questions.prompt: Should BC expand care without consent for people in severe mental health or addiction crises?
questions.yes: Expand care without consent for severe crises.
questions.no: Do not expand care without consent.
questions.note: The parties propose different admission rules. Their safeguards and treatment plans need separate scrutiny.

stances.summary: Supports more involuntary care beds for severe crises.
Proposes mandatory care interventions.
Supports medically supervised admission when legal criteria are met.
Proposes involuntary rehabilitation for severe addiction.

questions.prompt: Should BC change to proportional representation?
questions.yes: Allocate seats more closely to parties’ share of the vote.
questions.no: Keep choosing one MLA per riding by the most votes.
questions.note: Proportional systems vary. A commitment to introduce legislation does not settle the final voting system.

stances.summary: Would introduce proportional representation legislation.
